title: Robust Structure Learning of $k$-local Lindbladians
authors: Tim Möbus, Thiago Bergamaschi, Daniel Stilck França, Cambyse Rouzé
abstract: We present an efficient protocol for learning an unknown $k$-local Lindblad generator on $n$ qubits using only product-state preparations, short-time evolution, and single-qubit Pauli measurements, without prior knowledge of the interaction structure. For fixed $k$ and bounded weighted interaction strength, the protocol estimates all Hamiltonian and dissipative Pauli--GKSL coefficients to entrywise accuracy $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-δ$ using $\widetilde{\mathcal O}_k(\varepsilon^{-2}n^{2k}\log(1/δ))$ samples and polylogarithmically many evolution times. A semidefinite projection converts these estimates into a valid $k$-local Lindblad generator with diamond-norm error at most $\varepsilon$ using $\widetilde{\mathcal O}_k(\varepsilon^{-2}n^{4k}\log(1/δ))$ samples and polynomial-time classical postprocessing. If a suitable set of influential coefficients is supplied and satisfies a stable sparsity condition, the dependence on $n$ can improve from polynomial to logarithmic; in particular, exact supports of bounded intersection degree require only $\widetilde{\mathcal O}_k(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(n/δ))$ samples, with analogous reductions in system-size dependence for sufficiently decaying long-range interactions. We also provide a robust structure-learning procedure, extend the guarantees to model misspecification, and prove complementary sample-complexity lower bounds. To our knowledge, these are the first efficient learning guarantees for general $k$-local dissipative quantum dynamics under such limited experimental control.
summary: This paper presents novel, efficient protocols for learning the generator of open quantum system dynamics (Lindbladians) using only limited measurements like product-state preparations. By combining advanced techniques such as Semidefinite Programming with structural assumptions on interactions, it achieves rigorous sample complexity guarantees that scale favorably with system size $n$ when the underlying physics is sparse or local.
main_problem: The core problem is developing efficient, data-driven protocols to reconstruct an unknown $k$-local Lindbladian generator ($\mathcal{L}$) governing open quantum system dynamics.
main_result: The authors provide sample complexity bounds for learning the coefficients of $\mathcal{L}$ using limited measurements, achieving significant improvements when exploiting sparsity assumptions. They also establish lower bounds proving the necessity of these sample complexities.
method: The methodology combines techniques from quantum process tomography (using product-state preparations and short-time evolution) with advanced mathematical tools like Semidefinite Programming (SDP) to project noisy estimates onto the space of physically valid Lindblad generators.
model_or_system: The system is an open quantum system of $n$ qubits evolving under a Markovian master equation, $ rac{d}{dt}ho(t) = \mathcal{L}(ho(t))$. The generator $\mathcal{L}$ is assumed to be $k$-local, meaning interactions are confined to small subsets of qubits.
key_observables: The primary observables are the Pauli-GKSL coefficients ($\chi_{P,Q}$) defining the Lindbladian structure, and the measured quantities are related to the Pauli Transfer Matrix (PTM) elements derived from short-time evolution.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the accuracy $\epsilon$, failure probability $\delta$, locality $k$, system size $n$, and the weighted intersection strength $\alpha$ which bounds local interactions.
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes a constant bound on the interaction strength ($\alpha=O(1)$) for general learning, and relies heavily on exploiting sparsity structures (e.g., via supplied influential coefficients $\Omega$) to improve scaling from polynomial to logarithmic in $n$.
paper_structure: The paper develops a multi-stage pipeline: first, estimating raw coefficients from measurements; second, using SDPs to project these estimates onto the space of valid Lindbladians; and finally, deriving rigorous sample complexity bounds (both upper bounds for the protocol and lower bounds proving their necessity) based on locality assumptions.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides the theoretical tools necessary to characterize complex quantum dynamics in realistic settings where full tomography is impossible. The focus on $k$-locality and sparsity directly addresses resource limitations inherent in experimental quantum physics.
